items.text: Content: each brand can now set the languages its site is written in, a default language, and where each page type goes on the site (section, address pattern, layout to follow). A new page then gets its language and address by itself. Set it under Content settings on the Content page.
Funnels, trends and the other analytics pages no longer answer "internal error" when the database has no shared memory left for a parallel query: the question is asked again in a way that needs none.

Zeropark cost and targets: a traffic source that passes the campaign's long id ({long_campaign_id}) is now matched to Zeropark by it. Until now the short {campaign_id} number was used even then, which Zeropark refuses, so no cost or targets arrived.

New customer revenue can count a customer's signup from any of several events (`start_events`), so signups recorded under another event name, such as dates brought in from an earlier system, count too. The report page lets you add more than one signup event.
Security improvements to sign-in.

Brand search: a competitor whose name is a common word is no longer credited with every search for that word. Each competitor's domain is read beside its name, and a name searched far more than its domain, against the other names you follow, is marked "common word" and counted by an estimate. It needs five followed names to compare.

A click or sign-up tracked on an ad's landing page no longer starts a second visit without the ad's click id, so paid visits are counted once and keep their click id. In the paid ads report, a paused campaign whose customer paid again keeps its row, so the rows add up to the totals.

A brand can now keep each tracker click's full referrer, full user agent and IP address: turn each on under Tracker, Setup, and choose how many days to keep them. They show in the click log and as three new breakdowns in the Report. All three are off until you turn them on, and turning one off deletes what was kept.

Tracker report: percentages now show two decimals (5.00%). Grouped by offer, the clicks that never went on to an offer are named "No offer reached" instead of "(none)", and an offer's lander views, lander clicks and lander CTR are left blank, because every click with an offer came through a lander click and the rate always read 100%.

Removing a partner now comes with your removal email picked and shown as that partner will get it. A program remembers its removal notice, and if you have none yet you can create one in the same dialog from a starting wording, then reword it under Templates.

Your server can now name the tracker click a person came from: send `properties.ofclk` with their `userId`, and the browser that landed with that click joins them, so a funnel follows one person from the ad click into your app. Funnels with a very busy first step no longer time out, and the events list refuses too large a page clearly.

A new alert, Campaign tracking stopped: when a tracker campaign keeps getting clicks but its page loads or its conversions, which came steadily before, have stopped, the owners and admins hear once, so a removed snippet or a silent conversion feed is caught the same day instead of in next week's report.

Paid ads now shows what each Google campaign bids on: its custom goal and the conversion actions in it, or its standard goals. Conversions by type also counts an action in campaigns that don't bid on it, so you can see what Google credits beyond what bidding learns from.

The conversion send log now says which click each conversion went with and where the click id came from. When an ad platform refuses a conversion because its click is too old, Outflare sends it once more without the click id, so it can still be matched on the person's hashed email or phone.

Your site's own server can now report the ad clicks it sees arrive (`POST /v1/site/landings`). Tracking health then shows, per network, how many clicks reached your site but never ran the website script, and how many of them were crawlers.

Suggestions in the Tracker: Outflare now finds the placements of a network campaign whose clicks don't load your page while the campaign's other placements' do, lists them with their clicks and cost, and blocks them on the network when you press Accept change. Nothing changes until you accept, and any placement can be resumed from Targets.

A new alert, Conversions look arranged: when nearly all of a tracker campaign's conversions come from one placement or publisher that sends a small part of its clicks, and those clicks look alike (the same browser every time, or the same wait from click to conversion), the owners and admins hear once, so scripted or rewarded conversions are caught before more are paid for.

A Vercel connection can now take your site's request log from a log drain. Outflare keeps one landing per page request that carried a click id (an ad network's, or one of your own campaign links') with the status the visitor got, and drops the rest unread, so you see which paid clicks arrived but never ran the page. Turn it on under Connectors, Vercel, Live updates.

The conversion send log now shows the click id itself and the day of the click when the click id came from the ad platform's own cookie. It showed the whole cookie value and the day of the visit before.

A Sales conversation now opens as a deal-style page: who it is, their company, state and owner on top, then tabs for Chats (the thread with the reply box), Tasks, Notes, People at the company, Meetings and More. Add to sequence stays in the header on every tab, and only Sales managers see who opened a conversation.

The tracker has a Settings page: campaign names, the tracking domain, click filter rules, IP lookups and full click details sit on one page with a list on the left. New there is a naming template for campaigns, such as `{source} - {brand} - {date}`, so every new campaign of a brand starts with the same kind of name.

Click filters can be grouped under named rules, such as "Known scrapers" or "Our office", and each rule switched off and on again without losing what is in it. Find them under Tracker, Setup, Click filters.

The tracker has a Dashboard: your clicks, conversions, revenue, cost, profit and ROI against the period before, a day-by-day chart, the campaigns losing money, bot and suspect clicks, and your best campaigns, sources, offers, landers, countries and devices. Every number opens the Report on it.

Tracker reports can be grouped and filtered by the extra values a conversion's postback carried (p1 to p20), such as a plan, a product or a sub id from your affiliate network, so you can see which of them your revenue comes from.

Tracker reports can be grouped and filtered by connection type (mobile, residential, data centre and so on) and by zip or postal code, for the clicks your IP lookup connection checked. Both come from your own IPQualityScore account, at no extra lookups.

Clickadu and Evadav are ready-made traffic sources in the click tracker: their click id and up to 15 details of each click (zone, campaign, creative, place, device, connection type and more) are filled in for you.
Adcash is a ready-made traffic source in the click tracker: its click id, cost and 15 details (zone, campaign, creative, place, device and more) are filled in for you.

The Zeropark traffic source template now captures ten more values from each click: traffic type, keyword match, visitor type, target URL, browser, carrier, region, city, device ID and the campaign's UUID. New Zeropark traffic sources get them; for an existing one, add the parameters you want on its page.

The tracker's Report filters rows by their numbers (Profit under 0, Visits at least 100), compares every number with the period before, and has ready-made reports to start from, such as Campaigns losing money and Spend with no conversions. Saved views keep all of it.

Write to job candidates from your own work mailbox, inside the application. Start from a template that fills in the candidate and the job, change the text, and send. Rejecting someone opens the email for you to read first, and their status changes only once it has gone out. Only a person sends: no agent or token can email a candidate.

Costs & capacity shows what each paid tool has left, what it spent today, in 7 and in 30 days, and how long it lasts at that rate. Outflare warns you when a tool runs low, and at once when one runs out; for a provider that doesn't report a balance, type it after a top-up.

Sales reporting no longer reads a Lead Portal connection. Tools & spend lists what Outflare booked for the sales tools (AI, verification, sending, mailboxes, domains) for today, the last 7 and the last 30 days, Sales mailbox capacity comes from the brand's own mailboxes, and a build with its own discovery flow fills Discovery, its search lanes and Agent performance from its records.
